text:
devin: Heads-up — over the last 12h we've had a small spike where streaming sessions show duplicate 'active connections' in the console and double-counted route tokens. Noticed after the canary yesterday.

jess: ugh, any correlation with the resume/reconnect rollout? which proxy was in the path?

devin: looks correlated with the new edge-proxy that adds `x-rd-request-id` and rewrites `x-forwarded-for`. Repro steps: start a ws client, kill conn, reconnect quickly (<500ms). Console shows 2 active sessions for same tenant-route.

maria: is the request-id namespace stable across reconnects? we expect `resume_id` to be canonical key.

devin: that's the suspect — proxy sometimes assigns a new `x-rd-request-id` on reconnect and the resume token is accepted but the console aggregation groups by request-id for session counts. So telemetry and billing get split.

rahul: that would cause sample skew too — dashboards use request-id tag to join streaming metrics. If request-id changes mid-session, we've been counting two sessions. :grimacing:

sam: can you paste the minimal headers dump?

devin: sure — snippet from the client repro logs:

```
GET /v1/stream?route=foo HTTP/1.1
Host: inference.redwood.internal
Connection: Upgrade
Upgrade: websocket
Sec-WebSocket-Key: ...
x-rd-request-id: r-abc123
x-resume-id: resume-42
x-tenant-id: team-7
```

(reconnect)

```
GET /v1/stream?route=foo HTTP/1.1
x-rd-request-id: r-def456    # proxy replaced
x-resume-id: resume-42
```

maria: so resume-id stayed the same but request-id changed. Who owns request-id assignment? edge-proxy or the client?

devin: edge-proxy in canary replaced it when connection came from a different NAT mapping. We now think the proxy treats reconnect as a new request and generates a fresh request-id.

jess: console rule is grouping sessions by `x-rd-request-id` for per-connection metrics because it was cheap to implement. That was lazy. We should aggregate by `x-resume-id` when present, fall back to request-id.

rahul: agreed. But watch out: resume-ids can be replayed across sessions in rare edge cases, we need idempotency checks. Also affects billing path — token meter currently uses request-id in ingesters.

sam: quick patch idea: change streaming-metrics join key order -> `resume_id` then `request_id`. Also emit a `reconnect_count` metric if resume matches existing session.

devin: tried that locally — fixes console counts but exposes a second problem: some older proxies strip `x-resume-id` for preflight / early close and we lose the field. So we need a fallback and a migration plan.

maria: can we have the proxy preserve `x-resume-id` or echo it if present? that seems safest. Ops-team, is that feasible without rolling back canary?

ops-bot: deploy job queued: edge-proxy canary v3.8 -> revize header-preserve mode. ETA ~2h to test. :gear:

jess: timeline: short-term we should change console aggregation logic (non-breaking) and add a telemetry tag `reconnect=true` when resume_id seen on reconnect. Long-term, require header-preserve in proxy and update doc.

rahul: also add a safety check in billing pipeline: if two consecutive sessions share resume_id within Xs and same tenant-route, collapse token counts into the earlier session id to avoid double billing. We should backfill for last 24h anomalies too.

sam: I'll open a quick PR to switch aggregation key and add a feature flag. Keep it off until ops-bot confirms proxy change.

devin: opened https://git.redwood/streaming/PR/412 — contains console-side change + unit tests. Results: local + integration pass.

maria: can someone run a small query to find potential customers affected? query: `group by tenant, route where reconnect_count > 0 and session_pair_dup = true` on telemetry-24h.

jess: running a light query now, will post numbers in ~10m.

ops-bot: canary rollback ready if needed.

devin: thanks. TL;DR: root cause = request-id namespace mutation at proxy on reconnect; short-term console/telemetry should prefer resume_id for aggregation; long-term make proxy preserve resume_id and add billing dedupe logic.

maria: agreed. also add a note in rollout UX doc so PMs know consoles can show transient duplicates during rollout.

jess: noted. cc @pm-ux

sam: will ship PR behind feature flag and add a dashboard annotation for the canary window.

devin: leaving logs from reproducer in /var/tmp/sse-repro-4190001234.log — ping me if you need the script.

rahul: thanks all. low-severity but billing impact so prioritize the patch + probe backfill.

ops-bot: incident created: INC-2024-767 (low-sev) — assigned to eng-platform.
